newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures took their lead from German and U.S. bond markets again on Wednesday, settling lower after a relatively volatile session in which U.S. economic data set the tone.

The December bond future remained in a narrow range near the day's highs until a rise in U.K. interest rates unsettled European bond markets. Then a positive reaction in the U.S. to third quarter gross domestic product took the French contract back to the highs above 126.50.
Traders said a large sell order from a French brokerage late in the session then sent the contract into negative ground.

Jitters over the eligibility of the France Telecom transfer of pension fund assets to government coffers, designed to help reduce the French public deficit in 1997, faded allowing the franc to move back above 3.38 per mark.
Analysts said the political imperative of starting monetary union on time, with France on board, made it unlikely that the European Commission would prevent the transfer in the end.

"There's going to be some horse-trading but ultimately France is in a good position as it knows Germany doesn't want to give up on monetary union," David Brickman, European economist at Yamaichi International.
A foreign exchange trader at a French bank said Japanese investors had been selling marks and moving into other European currencies such as the franc and the lira.

He said although he thought there was scope for the franc to slip as low as 3.3850, as some institutions which had borrowed in francs were looking to unwind their positions, the French unit would remain trapped between 3.3780 and 3.3820 for now.
Another trader in Paris said French corporates had been selling marks for francs earlier today.
The rebound in the franc helped December PIBOR settle unchanged ahead of a Bank of France policy meeting on Thursday.

A bond analyst at a French bank said the recent strength of the franc and the convergence between German and French bond yields at the short end gave the Bank of France a window of opportunity to cut its intervention rate from 3.25 percent.

"The move at the two-year part of the curve is continuing the convergence seen all along the curve, it's now at its lowest level this year," he said. "The franc is well supported so there's no problem from a market point of view."
Although there will be no Bank of France money market tender on Thursday because of a holiday on Friday, any change in rates will be announced at the normal time of 1315 GMT.
Hopes for French easing helped December PIBOR outperform December Euromarks. The spread narrowed to 33 basis points, the lowest level this year.
Some analysts said French September unemployment figures, which economists polled by Reuters expected to show a 15,000 monthly rise, could also prompt the Bank of France to cut rates tomorrow.
In a Reuter poll of 20 economists published on Tuesday 15 said they expected a cut in the intervention rate this week.
